title: Very good clone, moderate longevity
text:
Grand Parfums Versace Eros opens with a strong projection of citrus, fruity, sweet, musky and spicy notes. The opening is very fresh, sharp, bright, inviting, unique, and delectable. The green apple, mint, ambroxan, and lemon are the most prominent opening notes. The lemon is the fresh and bright opening note, astringent, sour, and vibrant; the green apple is by its side, delectable, sweet, sour, crispy, and acidic. The mint rounds up the opening with its cooling green and slightly spicy note. The ambroxan is also noticeable musky, lemony, and ambery note that works well, improving the fragrance's projection. As the fragrance moves towards its dry down, the tonka bean and vanilla add a sweet and aromatic touch without making the fragrance overly sweet or taking the focus away from the mint, green apple, and lemon. The vetiver, oakmoss, and cedar are part of the support notes; they combine their notes to create a fresh green and woody accord but remain in the back of the fragrance. The fragrance is linear, all notes come up as soon as the fragrance is applied and continue into the dry down. Once Grand Parfums Versace Eros has reached its full dry down, it can be summarized as a strong projection, spicy mint, fruity green apple, musky ambroxan, mildly sweet vanilla, tonka, and woody cedar fragrance. The fragrance feels casual, comforting, delectable, energizing, exquisite, fresh, fruity, green, high-quality, inviting, masculine, modern, musky, nicely-blended, playful, refreshing, rich, sharp, seductive, sour, sparkly, special, sweet, unique, versatile, wild, woody, and very pleasant.

CATEGORY: Aromatic fougere
BATCH REVIEWED: 2019.
WOW RATING: 10/10. A deliciously sweet, fresh spicy, fruity, musky, and woody fragrance.
DISLIKE RATING: 0/10. The fragrance contains no offensive or harsh notes.
UNIQUENESS: 10/10. The notes are relatively common, but the resulting scent is unique.
MASS APPEAL: 10/10. A delectable fragrance, a crowd-pleaser.
PROJECTION: 6/10. Very good, about 6 feet around the wearer.
SILLAGE: 8/10. Impressive, about 8 feet behind the wearer.
APPLICATION: 4-6 atomizations.
LONGEVITY: 5/10. Good, about 5 hours, it projects well for over 3 hours.
CLONE RATING: 10/10. A great clone, the original has a more noticeable ambroxan which develops into a dry accord. In this fragrance the fruity, mint, and lemon and stronger than the ambroxan.
SEASONS: Winter, spring, summer, fall, colder days, daytime, nighttime, and climate-controlled environments.
OCCASIONS: Outdoor gatherings, gym, sports, office, casual, holidays, vacations, romantic, dating, clubbing. This is an office-friendly fragrance.
VERSATILITY: 10/10. A highly versatile fragrance that can be worn any time of the year and occasion.
GENDER: Masculine. The spicy mint creates a slight tilt to the masculine side. I can safely be worn as unisex.
AGES: Any.
RECOMMENDATION: Grand Parfums Versace Eros can be purchased for about $27(8oz). It is a delectable, unique, and very inviting fragrance which makes it the ideal crowd-pleaser. This is a great buy.
BLIND-BUY: Yes.

• Montale Starry Nights features apple, lemon, patchouli and roses, a fantastic and very different fragrance.
• Parfums De Marly Layton EDP is a great, intense, spicy, cardamom, sweet, vanilla, guaiac wood, lavender, fruity, apple, and sandalwood fragrance.
• Salvatore Ferragamo F Black Pour Homme EDT is a good, fresh, woody, and peppery fragrance.
• Versace Eros EDT is a fantastic, spicy mint, fruity green apple, musky ambroxan, mildly sweet vanilla, tonka, and woody cedar fragrance.
• Versace Eros Flame EDP is fantastic, intense, citrus chinotto, lemon, mandarin orange, spicy black pepper, rosemary, mildly sweet, tonka, vanilla, and woody cedar fragrance.
• Victoria Secret Very Sexy Platinum for Him is OK, very common, a fresh woody, mossy, ozonic, violet leaf, and spicy fragrance.
• Grand Parfums Versace Eros is a fantastic, intense, spicy mint, fruity green apple, musky ambroxan, mildly sweet vanilla, tonka, and woody cedar fragrance.

title: Horrible, Horrible, Nasty Juice
text: This perfume confuses me so much. I really want to like it. Looking at the notes, I should be crazy about it. Yet every time I try it on, I am tempted to scrub it off. I get a strongly unpleasant alcohol-like blast when I spritz it on. After a few minutes that is gone but what replaces it is not much better. To describe it I would say imagine lighting a big pile of pencil shavings on fire, and then threow in a couple of cloves and a couple of wilted gardenia petals, and the smoke from this concoction burning would be what this scent smells like on me. That is all I smell until after a couple of hours, at which point I can smell nothing unless I bring my wrist to my nose. On my wrist I smell a powdery, perfume-that's-so-old-its-turned-to-alcohol smell. Sadness. I guess I should be glad that the longevity and sillage on me are both horrible. Why can't this perfume be nice to me? I'm not giving up this easily, though. I think I'm going to try layering it with other scents. I don't think I could do anything to make it worse.  I definitely do NOT recommend.

title: Thouq by Lattafa is a Clone of P.D.M.D.E!!!!
text: Oh my goodness, you all would not believe me if I was to tell you that......."Thouq" by Lattafa Pride Collection is the clone of "Perfume De Marly Delina Exclusif"!!! I couldn't believe it when I first smelled the sample of "Thouq" when I received it in my previous order for "Al Fursan Unlimited" by Lattafa and immediately grabbed my sample from "Scent Bird" from my perfume sample box and smelled the two together.😄 They are exactly the same, the only thing I can say is that "Thouq" has a weird plastic chemical smell when you open the package and when you spray it. Be forewarned,  let the package air out by an open window or outside and also, spray it about 5 to 8 times to get that chemical smell out of the bottle before spraying it on yourself, It can be headache 😫 inducing. Also, the juice "inside" is a "dark amber" color, meaning it will stain your clothes. Once you get pass all of that, that's when you will get that creamy rose,  litchi, amber and vetiver. As you can see in my photo, that I have all (3) as my testimony. Thouq is 95% dupe of "Perfume De Marly Delina Exclusif" in comparison. Please, just be mindful of the strong chemical smell from the packaging and inside the juice. Spray it 5 to 8 times and let it macerate for a while and then come back to it. Otherwise, I really love this perfume.

title: Thouq
text: I saw a short review online from a fairly popular perfume reviewer on YouTube and many of his videos are featured on Amazon as well. But I really was curious to try Thouq after he compared it to Delina Exclusif which has become a crowd pleaser over the past year. I can see why so many love it after testing it while on vacation but the price point was extremely high! Long story short, I quickly purchased Thouq which was delivered within one week. All I can say is it's a beautiful rose scent enveloped in a slightly woody and sweet notes. It's quite strong and last forever which is common with Lattafa perfumes. Having said that, I would probably only wear this on cooler spring or fall days. It seems too heavy for warmer weather.

title: Not ideal for very pale skin, but usable
text:
For the record, I am a longtime Physicians Formula wearer, and their products can be hit or miss. I am not being paid to leave a review, or representing anyone but myself here. This is the first time I tried PF's countouring powder, and I've used it for about three seasons. I like it. I don't love it.

I have very pale skin with pink undertones that is uber-sensitive and I have to be very careful about sun exposure. Anything can make me break out in hives or eczema, at any time, even if I used it daily for years. Thankfully, PF products have never done that to me, in almost a decade.

As for this product, the shades are where I take some issue. They worked best for my tone in summer, but now, in winter -- I'm shopping for a different product.

* The dark shade is really mahogany-like, so I have to blend, blend, blend in daylight or risk looking like I smeared mud on my face. It's good for shading jawline and cheekbones with a light touch at temples if you need it. Beware, though. If you are very pale, you want a very light touch with this one.

*The medium shade is very subtle and helps blend and soften the dark. It also works well as a matte bronzer, around sides of the nose, and wherever you need just a little definition. This is the best shade of the bunch, honestly. At least for my skin tone.

* The light shade is, frankly, worthless to me. It gives my skin a pasty, chalky look and looks heavy. Yuck. I occasionally use it in tiny spots as a concealer, but as a contour powder, it just looks like I put on way too much setting powder or something. Instead, I use my lightest shade of matte eyeshadow (also a PF product) and a higher-end illuminator for highlighting. Those results are beautiful, frankly, even on my 38 year old skin.

All in all, PF's contour colors are suitable for pale skin, but may be better on other slightly darker or warmer skin tones, or on summer tanned skin.

title: If you wear it right, it stays and looks great!
text:
This is a thin liquid product that dries on and is extremely pigmented. There is a right and wrong way to apply it!

First and foremost, be sure that you are hydrated and your lips are not chapped at all. Any cracks or dryness will be emphasized once you apply this product.

Also, as tempting as it is, don't use chapstick or balm with this product. If you want moisture and shine, pick a different lipstick or use a drying gel on top. As long as your lips are moisturized and there is no oil or grease on them, you will be able to eat (carefully), drink, and smoke with no transfer at all.

You'll see it doesn't look perfect - that's because I was not careful putting it on (I'm just testing it at home) and it was dry before I could fix it. So do keep that in mind! I would also recommend a black lip liner on the edges for a cleaner look.

title: My "can't live without" product

It goes on smooth, and the tip is like a typical lip gloss applicator. But it is not forgiving (it will temporarily stain your regular skin if you're not careful!), it is forever. Once you put it on just hang out with your mouth open for 30 seconds for it to seal in, and then you're good to go, with drinks and everything, for at least my usual 5-hour stint.

At the end of the day, this lipstick does smudge off, or even wash off: it flakes off. Which is kind of amazing since I don't use makeup remover: I just rub my lips against each other, or rub them with a paper towel or washclothes and the whole thing comes off easily.

NOTE: Your lips will feel dry by the end of the night because they will be, but you CANNOT add a lip gloss or chapstick atop this lipstick or it will completely lose its efficacy as a stay-put product: it will move around and stain everything—I learned this the hard way.

Almost every pic on my Instagram (@ojanmarie) has me wearing this excellent shade, which is a true red, on the slightly blue-red side, but not bright like a tomato, much deeper and more saturated than that. It will go on your lips a lighter shade and will dry darker, just FYI.

Good luck using my fav product!!!

title: Practice and Time.
text:
if you've never used this before, be aware! this takes some practice. and time. but it's worth it!

i heat it up in the microwave, for about 10sec, then spread it out in a layer on wax paper to cool and reset. the cooling time is short, but the resetting time is longer, if you are going to apply at 5pm i'd melt and set at around noon to ensure it's fully set and strong enough to pull off the wax paper without tearing, also to diminish the stickiness of the previously melted product.

enjoy!

title: Super Finicky, Super Sticky
text: I bought this because I wanted to try FX grade gelatin for its strength and durability rather than use my homemade mixes and risk it melting under theatrical lights or tearing etc. The cubes are smaller than I expected but that was fine for my small prosthetics. First off the gelatin takes hours to set firm. I recommend refrigerating your pieces if you can. Yet even after a night in the fridge the piece was extremely sticky, very delicate and some parts were just plain gummy and not set at all. This can happen if the gelatin is boiled as that breaks down the chemicals. On the second try I took care to not let it boil at all, same result. The only pro is that it takes color tint very well. A bit of creme make up will do the trick. Make your own gelatin at home for the same price. Mines not sticky, it sets fast and decently durable. I will be trying other brands of fx cubes as well.

title: Mild yet powerful cleansing oil
text:
This is what I use as the first step to my night time skin care routine. It is a gentle yet powerful cleansing oil that effectively removes layers of sunscreen, waterproof mascara, liquid eyeliner, liquid glitter eyeshadow, and eyebrow pomade at once. I haven’t tried this with liquid foundation yet, so I cannot say much about it’s ability to remove a full-face make-up.

What I love about it is the texture. It is not a watery nor a heavy type of cleansing oil. It is rather lightweight that easily glides onto the skin for a gentle massage. Two pumps of this cleansing oil is enough to cleanse my entire face thoroughly without leaving any traces of waterproof make-up and sunscreen. It also doesn’t leave any greasy or sticky residue.

On its own, it is a hydrating and refreshing cleanser. I have an oily skin, so I love how I feel very refreshed after using this; it helps remove excess oil and unclog my pores. I noticed that my nose where I have the most blackheads is clearer than before.

Rather than using cleansing wipes, I have always used cleansing oils and balms because these truly remove make-up and sunscreen. I also love that cleansing oils and balms are environmentally-friendly without leaving any wastes. However, not all cleansing oils and balms are created equal. I feel that this A24 cleansing oil is very luxurious due to its premium ingredients. It is the only cleansing oil that I have tried that can be used on its own without a second or follow-up foam/gel cleanser.

I strongly recommend this product to anyone in need of a cleansing oil for hydration and thorough removal of make-up and sunscreen.

title: Great two-in-one makeup remover & cleanser
text: I love this cleanser. It’s a great one-stop-shop to remove makeup and wash my face. The oil removes liquid eyeliner and mascara, along with foundation. It leaves my skin feeling clean and fresh—and the best part is I don’t need a second cleanser to remove that oily makeup remover feeling I get with other products. The smell is mild, and though I have sensitive skin, this oil to foam cleanser is safe and gentle.

title: Works great!
text: I bought this to replace a different oil cleanser that went out of stock and I’m really happy with the product. It removes eye makeup, including mascara, and my foundation. It has a refreshing citrus scent that’s mild and not overwhelming. I like that it only uses clean, natural ingredients. I have sensitive skin and this felt nice on my skin—and didn’t cause a reaction like so many products out there do.

title: Softens skin, it's not greasy.
text: I am using this because of the deep cleaning claim and not to remove makeup. I live in the mountains where it is windy and dry, and I have mild eczema so I am always battling dry skin. I really had my doubts that an oil based product could clean my skin... well, I just discovered that yes it can! I am probably not using it as directed, as I like to wet wash my face while I am in the shower. Standing over my bathroom sink just makes too much of a mess. When it first lathers up it sort of has a smell like citronella, which I am not fond of, but I found that smell to quickly dissipate, and end up smelling quite nice and fresh, and not greasy. My skin feels soft and clean after using this product. It it was a larger bottle i might use it up on the rest of my dry skin body, if it wasn't so costly! (Sorry, TMI!)

title: Nice
text: I have been using a cleansing oil as step one in a double cleanse routine for 20 years now. Back then there was only one company from Japan that made such a thing that was available in the US. So for years, that is what I used. I decided to try this product simply to try something new. It has the same consistency as my normal cleansing oil, but didn't seem to lather or clean as well. It also left my skin feeling oily despite how much a rinsed it away.  It has a fresh, citrus scent and the bottle size it a tad bit bigger than my normal. That being said, I liked this product but probably would not purchase to use again. The cost is higher and I can't get past the fact it doesn't clean off makeup that well.

title: Very mild and worked out great for my oily sensitive skin.
text:
I requested this cleansing oil due to its claim on natural ingredients (99.75%).
First of all, I have an oily combination skin type that gets sensitive depending on my hormonal cycle. So naturally I have been hesitant to use any oil type skin care products on my face.
But I have learned that using an oily skin cleanser will not produce more oil on your skin, instead, a good oil cleanser is designed to balance and remove everything but skin's moisture.
So I have been searching for one to try out. Since this one is my first cleansing oil, I don’t have any experience with other cleansing oils to compare this with. So my impression about this is as a general cleansing product whether oil or otherwise.
The bottom line is that I liked how it worked on removing make-ups and how my skin felt afterwards. It didn’t feel heavy on my oily skin and felt soft and clean after washing my face following this.

title: This Makeup Remover Really Works!
text:
This A24 Cleansing Oil really works! I usually use baby oil to remove makeup, but this A24 Cleansing Oil
was even more effective! Like the baby oil, it is hypoallergenic. However, this cleansing oil does not contain mineral oil, a petroleum product. Instead, it contains USDA-approved organic Aloe Vera leaf juice. Camellia Japonica Seed Oil, Shea, Safflower oil, jojoba oil, avocado oil, Argan oil, Macadamia seed oil, olive oil, marigold, green tea, chamomile, horsetail, acai, lavender, ginseng, rosemary, sage, comfrey, nettle, quinoa, orange peel oil and grapefruit peel oil. All good things! And no water is added.

This wonderfully effective oil is also great because of the ingredients it does not contain! There are no parabens, silicones, phthalates, alcohol or artificial colors or fragrances.

This awesome makeup remover is made in the United States.

There is a different shadow in my inner corner but the rest of the lid is the DGAF on top of regular eyeshadow.
I decided to give it 3 stars because of the good formula, the fact it pressed back together so it's still usable, and because you can still get a good look from it, it's a gorgeous color.
I would've rated this 5 stars if it wasn't because the product was broken. Shame.

text: It's very very difficult to find a hypoallergic dark purple eyeliner that has a small enough applicator to make a thin line, stays on, and yet comes off before bedtime only when I take it off. I have been searching for this for decades. I was so excited when gel came out, but the brushes are never thin enough and pencils don't make thin enough lines. With sharpeners, you lose a lot of product and they never get as sharp as when new or you just lose the whole tip. Forget regular pencil eyeliners, same prob, but I can't use those anyway b/c no color comes off on my eye; it's like trying to use an actual crayon. I would have given this 5 stars, but I can't put it near the corner of my eye b/c it just ends up IN my eye, but at least it's not as irritating as any others, and that's probably just my own crazy sensitivity--I can get close enough that it looks good. Mind you, I'm only putting it under the lashes and NOT on the inner lid rim. Plus, I have been given the tip to wipe off excess before application, but I think as I age my damn eyes have gotten more sensitive. I have searched for years. I have mostly green hazel eyes, and dark purple is the only thing that doesn't make my eyes look brown. I've used this for a month or so, so I highly recommend it!

title: Incredible stuff.
text:
I'm not going to be able to write enough good things to truly highlight the wonders of this product.

I bought it, frankly, on a whim. I've largely stuck to a narrow variety of men's body wash products over the last 15 years or so. But in recent years I'd been gradually trying to incorporate more natural, chemical-free products into my household, and happened to run across this on Amazon.

Surely many have wondered, just as surely as I did upon opening this package, what on earth Mr. Postman had just delivered to my house. Wow. It was this huge, chunky mass of...stuff...with a very earthy smell.

I took about 1/2 cup of it and made a small bar of soap. It lathers very richly and has a very creamy texture. I use it also to shampoo and shaving cream.

I've been using it for about six months now and this is what I can say:

After the first few times I used it, it seemed to leave my skin dry. After about four days, that abated entirely. Within about 8 days, I thought I noticed something different about my skin quality, but I wasn't sure. After two weeks, the improvements could not be denied.

I've since given several away as gifts to friends and family. I can't imagine that I'll ever use any brand-name soaps ever again. I don't know why I would. This product cleans your skin. The cocoa pod and plantain skin ashes act as natural exfoliators, gradually revealing an evened skin tone and healthier skin. All these months later, my skin continues to improve.

Some complain about the smell of it, but I think it smells great. And 10 minutes after your shower, even what little scent remains quickly fades away. You can add essential oils if you'd like to get creative.

This is some really good soap. Get some for yourself and a few friends or to give as gifts. It lasts forever (between uses, put your bar someplace where it doesn't get water splashed on it or it will "melt").

I've since started using the raw shea butter as well, and using the products in tandem, man, I'll tell you! Unbelievable the results!

I bought the 1 pound package the first time. This is my second order. I recommend highly.

text: I bought this for my mother after reading reviews online from patients receiving radiation. She started using it 1 week prior to radiation on her face. She is only in the 2nd week of her treatments so will update later regarding her completed treatment. Update: Mom is on Day 13 of her radiation to her jaw/face and is experiencing mucositis and redness to her face. We are still using Miaderm and she is experiencing very little inflammation to her skin (on the outside). FYI: I showed the radiation oncologist Miaderm and he looked at the ingredients list and said it has alcohol do not use it.I told him it was developed by radiation oncologist and Phase III clinical trials. And that it was not the type of drying alcohol. He would not even listen to me. He said only use aquaform (which is a petroleum based product-YUCK)otherwise "you are going to come and say my skin is drying and blame me b/c I said it was okay to use" He needs a refresher on chemistry - Yes the word "alcohol" is in the ingredients list but it is ceteryl alcohol different from the fermented alcohol that is drying. After leaving the clinic,  I pulled up the ingredient list for Aquaform and it had "lanolin alcohol" as an ingredient.. again it is a fatty conditioning "alcohol" not the drying kind-- urgh I wish I had known this to show him aquaform ingredient list!! Do not let the arrogance of doctors stop you from finding the best product for you.It is unfortunate that we can't always have doctors who will take the initiative to learn about a new product, research it, and then give us their opinion rather than just dismissing the patient.  I don't expect doctors to know the newest and best products on the market, but I do expect them to be open to learning about new products that may be helpful to their clients.

title: Overly drying
text:
I received this product complimentary from Influenster and Yardley in exchange for my honest opinion.

I have used Yardley London bar soaps before; but it had been years, so I was looking forward to trying again. I always see them in my local dollar store and think they smell nice, but couldn't remember why I didn't buy them again.

Now I do.

Heavily fragranced, overly drying, and has added dyes. I do like that they are SOMEWHAT natural and that the packaging is earth friendly, but just cannot justify even spending a dollar on it when there are so many other great options for the same price. They feel almost misleading with their approach, like they want to appear more animal and earth friendly than they actually are. Product just doesn't match advertising.

The box states it also exfoliates, but I could not feel any exfoliating properties whatsoever. Left my skin extremely dry and flakey all over. This is a hard no for me.
